title: Q1 2026 Latency vs Cost: Microbench & Region Split (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This draft captures microbench results and simple cost extrapolations across hardware types and quantization profiles. Goal is to produce 1-2 slides for customer-facing collateral and a short internal recommendation for default model variant selection by region.

Test scope and constraints:
- Synthetic single-turn generation workloads only (no tool/function calls).
- Prompt size fixed at 32 tokens, generation target 256 tokens.
- Measured p50/p90/p99 latency, steady-state throughput (tokens/s), and estimated cost per 1M output tokens.
- Hardware: H100-80GB, A100-80GB, T4-32GB (spot-like).
- Models: redwood-1-4b (fp16), redwood-1-4b-int8 (nf4), r1-8b (fp16).
- Batching: continuous-batching enabled at batch sizes {1,4,8,16}, concurrency varied to saturate GPU.
- Region split: us-west1, eu-west1 — identical instance types but different observed queueing due to background load.

Raw numeric summary (representative run, 95% CI ±5%):
1) Latency percentiles (ms) — generation-only (prompt + decode 256 tokens). Columns: Model | HW | batch=1 p50/p90/p99 | batch=8 p50/p90/p99
- redwood-1-4b (fp16) | H100 | 82 / 140 / 380 | 120 / 210 / 540
- redwood-1-4b (nf4 int8) | H100 | 95 / 170 / 490 | 140 / 260 / 610
- r1-8b (fp16) | H100 | 160 / 300 / 900 | 240 / 420 / 1200
- redwood-1-4b (fp16) | A100 | 90 / 155 / 420 | 130 / 230 / 600
- redwood-1-4b (nf4) | A100 | 105 / 185 / 520 | 160 / 290 / 700
- redwood-1-4b (fp16) | T4  | 210 / 420 / 1500 | 420 / 950 / 2800

2) Steady-state throughput (tokens/s per GPU) — generation 256 tokens per request, batching applied:
- redwood-1-4b fp16 @ H100: batch=1 -> 1,800 t/s | batch=8 -> 12,200 t/s
- redwood-1-4b nf4 @ H100: batch=1 -> 1,550 t/s | batch=8 -> 10,600 t/s
- r1-8b fp16 @ H100: batch=1 -> 950 t/s | batch=8 -> 6,900 t/s
- redwood-1-4b fp16 @ A100: batch=1 -> 1,650 t/s | batch=8 -> 11,400 t/s
- redwood-1-4b fp16 @ T4:  batch=1 -> 600 t/s   | batch=8 -> 2,900 t/s

3) Estimated cost per 1M output tokens (USD) — using list prices and a simple amortized infra cost model (GPU hr $/hr): H100 $8.50/hr, A100 $3.50/hr, T4 $0.60/hr. Calculation: (GPU/hr) / (t/s * 3600s) * 1e6 + small overhead (0.02) for infra.
- redwood-1-4b fp16 @ H100 (batch=8): ~ $8.50 / (12200*3600) *1e6 + 0.02 ≈ $0.20 per 1k tokens -> $200 per 1M tokens (note: rough)
- redwood-1-4b nf4 @ H100 (batch=8): ≈ $230 per 1M tokens
- r1-8b fp16 @ H100 (batch=8): ≈ $400 per 1M tokens
- redwood-1-4b fp16 @ A100 (batch=8): ≈ $260 per 1M tokens
- redwood-1-4b fp16 @ T4  (batch=8): ≈ $1,600 per 1M tokens (inefficient for production)

Text charts (small ascii visualizations to show tradeoffs)
A) Latency tail tradeoff (p99) for redwood-1-4b across HW (batch=1):
H100  : |#####------| 380ms
A100  : |####-------| 420ms
T4    : |############| 1500ms
Scale: | 0----500----1000----1500 |

B) Cost vs median latency (normalized) for three configs (lower is better is cost & latency):
Config   | norm_cost | norm_p50 | quadrant
r1-4b H100 fp16 | 1.0 | 1.0 | fast+cheap
r1-4b H100 nf4  | 1.15| 1.16| slightly slower, slightly costlier
r1-8b H100 fp16 | 2.0 | 1.95| expensive, higher latency
(note: normalization anchored to r1-4b fp16 H100 batch=8)

Regional observations (us-west1 vs eu-west1):
- Baseline p50 on eu-west1 is ~8–12% higher than us-west1 for same instance types and load pattern. The most likely causes: inter-zone network variance + lower bursting headroom in eu region test cluster.
- Cost per 1M tokens ~ similar but turn-up time for new capacity in eu test pool is slower, impacting cold-start percentiles.

Anomalies and signals to investigate:
- p99 spikes for NF4 int8 on A100 observed in two runs: correlation with GC-like CUDA stalls in kernel logs. Action: capture nvprof traces and correlate with batching window alignment (ticket ENG-4231).
- T4 tail behavior is non-linear with concurrency > 16 — probably due to memory thrashing on KV cache.

Interpreting for product decisions (quick takeaways):
- For latency-sensitive endpoints (p99 < 500ms target): r1-4b fp16 on H100 (batch tuned to small-to-medium) is the clear winner. NF4 int8 is attractive for cost but introduces tail volatility; requires mitigations (micro-batching alignment, kernel scheduling).
- For cost-constrained workloads with relaxed tails: consider nf4 on A100 or H100 with aggressive caching and prefix reuse; but quantify p99 regression against SLOs.
- Avoid T4 for customer-facing low-latency generation at current workloads; acceptable for internal batch embedding pipelines.

Draft messaging for collateral (two sentences):
"Redwood's serving runtime delivers sub-120ms median latencies for 4B-class models on H100 at production batch rates, translating to unit economics below $250 per 1M generated tokens when combined with intelligent batching and caching. Quantized variants (NF4) can reduce compute cost but require careful scheduling to avoid tail-latency regressions—we recommend H100 NF4 for cost-optimized backends and FP16 H100 for latency-first APIs."

Open questions / next steps:
- Re-run NF4 kernel traces on A100/H100 with nvprof and store GPU profiles in S3 for ENG-4231 (owner: Marco).
- Run mixed chat-like workloads (multi-turn, variable prompt sizes) to see impact on KV cache reuse and amortized cost (owner: Aisha).
- Produce 2-slide customer deck: 1) latency vs cost chart + recommendation; 2) operational knobs (batching, cache, fallback) and typical tradeoffs (owner: Daniel).

Short action items (sprint next-steps):
- [ ] Capture nvprof traces for anomalous NF4 runs (Marco) — due 2026-02-18
- [ ] Create canonical script and docs to reproduce these microbench numbers (Aisha) — due 2026-02-20
- [ ] Draft 2-slide collateral and ops playbook (Daniel) — due 2026-02-25

Notes to reviewers:
- Numbers are intended for internal directional guidance; do not publish externally without finalizing the cost model (includes infra overheads, networking, and egress).
- If marketing wants a single headline number, recommend "~120ms median, ~ $200–300 per 1M tokens" for 4B-class on H100 with batching — but caveat with SLO and workload profiles.

Revision history:
- 2026-01-15 initial run and draft by Daniel
- 2026-01-22 added A100 runs and initial cost calc (Aisha)
- 2026-01-30 repeat runs after kernel build change, observed NF4 tail regressions (Marco)
- 2026-02-10 consolidated into this briefing for product/marketing review

End of draft.
